name: As a visitor, I want a combined changelog data feed so that agent update history can be surfaced consistently
desc:
## 🎯 TLDR

- **New pure data function `listChangelogEntries()`** in a new `lib/changelog.ts` — flattens every backlog agent's `updates[]` into one combined, newest-first feed.
- **Decoupled core logic**: an exported `buildChangelogFeed(agents: ChangelogSource[])` function takes a minimal fixture-friendly shape so it can be unit-tested without depending on the live registry singleton.
- **Normalizes data**: dates truncated to `YYYY-MM-DD`, missing/blank `author` defaults to `"unknown"`.
- This story is data-layer only — no UI changes. It is fully testable/valuable on its own as a reusable module other code (e.g. an upcoming `/changelog` page) can consume.

---

## 🔧 Technical Notes

- **Key files (new):** `lib/changelog.ts`, `tests/changelog.test.ts`
- **Reference files:** `lib/agent-registry.ts` (exports `backlogAgents`, `BacklogAgentManifest` type), `lib/backlog-meta.ts` (`AgentUpdate` type: `{ date: string; author: string; note: string }`), `lib/library-service.ts` (import/module style to mirror)
- **Types to add in `lib/changelog.ts`:**
  - `ChangelogEntry = { date: string; agentId: string; agentTitle: string; author: string; note: string }`
  - `ChangelogSource = Pick<BacklogAgentManifest, "id" | "title" | "updates">` (decouples the pure function from the registry singleton for testability)
- **Function behavior:**
  - `buildChangelogFeed(agents: ChangelogSource[]): ChangelogEntry[]` — `flatMap`s each agent's `updates[]` into `ChangelogEntry` objects.
  - Date normalization: `update.date.slice(0, 10)` (works whether source is already `YYYY-MM-DD` or a full ISO timestamp).
  - Author fallback: `update.author?.trim() || "unknown"`.
  - Sort: `b.date.localeCompare(a.date) || a.agentTitle.localeCompare(b.agentTitle)` (newest-date-first, same-date entries tiebroken by agent display name).
  - Export `listChangelogEntries(): ChangelogEntry[]` = `buildChangelogFeed(backlogAgents)` — the real entry point for consumers (e.g. the page).
- **Test style:** plain `describe`/`it`, fixture objects, no filesystem mocking — follow `tests/library-service.test.ts` / `tests/agent-registry.test.ts` conventions. Test `buildChangelogFeed` directly against fixture `ChangelogSource[]` arrays so the suite doesn't depend on real registry contents drifting over time.
- **Commands:** `npm run test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` must all pass after this story alone (the module is unused by any page yet, so no dead-import/dead-route risk — just a self-contained, exported, tested utility).

## 🚫 Out of Scope

- The `/changelog` page UI (separate story).
- Nav link and architecture doc updates (separate story).
- Adding `updates[]` support to shipped/library agents (`AgentLibraryEntry`) — flagged as a future consideration, not in scope here.

items: lib/changelog.ts exports ChangelogEntry and ChangelogSource types, buildChangelogFeed(agents), and listChangelogEntries()
buildChangelogFeed flattens each agent's updates[] into ChangelogEntry objects with agentId/agentTitle passed through unchanged
Dates are normalized to YYYY-MM-DD via slice(0, 10), working for both plain dates and full ISO timestamps
Missing/blank author falls back to "unknown" via update.author?.trim() || "unknown"
Feed is sorted newest-first by date, with same-date entries tiebroken by agentTitle (localeCompare)

tests/changelog.test.ts covers: no-updates agent contributes zero entries, same-date tiebreak by title, missing/blank author fallback, newest-first overall ordering across 3+ agents, ISO timestamp truncation
npm run test, npm run typecheck, and npm run lint all pass

name: As a visitor, I want a /changelog page so that I can browse all agent updates in one place
desc:
## 🎯 TLDR

- **New server component page `app/changelog/page.tsx`** rendering the combined changelog feed from `listChangelogEntries()`.
- **Reuses existing "Updates" list styling/tokens** from `app/backlog/[agentId]/page.tsx` — no new colors/spacing values, only existing CSS custom properties.
- **Each entry links back** to its agent's backlog detail page (`/backlog/{agentId}`), and the page renders an explicit empty state when there are zero entries.
- Page is reachable directly at `/changelog` (nav wiring is a separate story) — fully valuable and testable via manual visit / build on its own.

---

## 🔧 Technical Notes

- **Key files (new):** `app/changelog/page.tsx`
- **Depends on:** `lib/changelog.ts`'s `listChangelogEntries()` (prior story) — must be merged first.
- **Reference files:** `app/backlog/[agentId]/page.tsx` (~lines 210-235, the "Updates" section to mirror), `app/library/page.tsx` (empty-state pattern, e.g. "No matches yet"), `app/plan/page.tsx` / `app/backlog/[agentId]/page.tsx` for the overall page-chrome shape (`async function` default export, server component, no client state).
- **Page chrome:**
  - `<main className="page-wrap page-wrap-wide">`
  - `page-title` = "Changelog"
  - `page-subtitle` describing the combined feed across all backlog agents
- **Feed list markup** (mirrors backlog detail page's Updates block):
  - `<ul className="mb-0 mt-3 list-none space-y-4 p-0">`
  - `<li className="border-t border-[var(--rule-soft)] pt-4 first:border-t-0 first:pt-0">` per entry
  - Meta line: `{entry.date} · <Link href={`/backlog/${entry.agentId}`}>{entry.agentTitle}</Link> · {entry.author}` styled `text-[13.5px] font-medium text-[var(--ink-faint)]`
  - Note line styled `text-[15px] leading-6 text-[var(--ink-soft)]`
  - `key` combines `agentId` + `date` + array index (dates/agents can repeat, so index is required for uniqueness)
- **Empty state:** if `entries.length === 0`, render a "No updates yet" message (mirror `app/backlog/[agentId]/page.tsx`'s single-agent empty state, or `app/library/page.tsx`'s "No matches yet" pattern).
- **Commands:** `npm run test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and `npm run build` must all pass — the new route must build/render successfully even though it isn't linked from nav yet (Next.js App Router picks up any `page.tsx` under `app/` automatically, so the route is live at `/changelog` without any nav change).

## 🚫 Out of Scope

- Nav link wiring in `lib/garage-content.ts` (separate story).
- Architecture doc updates (separate story).
- Changes to `lib/changelog.ts` itself (already delivered).

name: Add Changelog page listing combined agent updates feed
desc:
## 🎯 TLDR

- **New data function `listChangelogEntries()`** in a new `lib/changelog.ts` — flattens every backlog agent's `updates[]` into one combined, sorted feed (newest first, agent name as tiebreaker), normalizing dates to `YYYY-MM-DD` and defaulting a missing author to `"unknown"`.
- **New page `app/changelog/page.tsx`** — server component, follows the exact structure/tokens of `app/backlog/[agentId]/page.tsx`'s existing "Updates" section (same list/border pattern), just fed by the combined feed instead of a single agent.
- **Nav link** added to `lib/garage-content.ts` `navGroups` (consumed by `components/portal-nav.tsx`) so `/changelog` shows up in the top nav automatically — no changes needed to `portal-nav.tsx` itself.
- **Scope note:** today only backlog manifests (`scoped`/`claimed`/`in_build`) carry an `updates[]` array — `AgentLibraryEntry` (shipped/library) has no `updates` field at all (see `lib/agent-library.ts`). "All agents in the registry" therefore means all `backlogAgents` (the only agents with update history). This mirrors how `registry/agents/codebase-onboarding-agent.yaml` and `registry/agents/project-memory-agent.yaml` are the only manifests with non-empty `updates` today.

---

## 📋 Implementation Steps

### Step 1: Add the `listChangelogEntries` data function
**Files:** `lib/changelog.ts` (new)

- Import `backlogAgents` and the `BacklogAgentManifest` type from `lib/agent-registry.ts` (same import style as `lib/library-service.ts`).
- Define a `ChangelogEntry` type: `{ date: string; agentId: string; agentTitle: string; author: string; note: string }`.
- Define a small `ChangelogSource` type (`Pick<BacklogAgentManifest, "id" | "title" | "updates">`) so the core function is decoupled from the live registry singleton and can be unit-tested with fixtures.
- Export a pure function `buildChangelogFeed(agents: ChangelogSource[]): ChangelogEntry[]` that:
  - `flatMap`s each agent's `updates[]` into `ChangelogEntry` objects.
  - Formats `date` to `YYYY-MM-DD` via `update.date.slice(0, 10)` (safe whether the source string is already `YYYY-MM-DD` or a full ISO timestamp).
  - Falls back to `"unknown"` when `author` is missing/blank: `update.author?.trim() || "unknown"` (guards against malformed data even though today's schema requires `author`; keeps the function robust and matches the requested test case).
  - Sorts newest first: `b.date.localeCompare(a.date) || a.agentTitle.localeCompare(b.agentTitle)` — this gives newest-date-first ordering with same-date entries tiebroken by agent display name (per the card).
- Export `listChangelogEntries(): ChangelogEntry[]` = `buildChangelogFeed(backlogAgents)` — this is what the page will call.

### Step 2: Unit tests for the data function
**Files:** `tests/changelog.test.ts` (new)

Follow the existing test style in `tests/library-service.test.ts` / `tests/agent-registry.test.ts` (plain `describe`/`it`, fixture objects, no mocking of the filesystem). Test `buildChangelogFeed` directly with fixture `ChangelogSource[]` arrays so the suite doesn't depend on real registry contents drifting over time. Cover:
- **No updates:** an agent with `updates: []` contributes zero entries to the feed.
- **Same-date tiebreak:** two agents each with one update on the same date — result is ordered by agent title (e.g. `"Alpha Agent"` before `"Zulu Agent"`), not by insertion order.
- **Missing/blank author:** an update whose `author` is `""` (or omitted, cast via fixture) renders as `"unknown"` in the resulting entry.
- **Newest-first overall ordering:** three agents with updates on different dates — result is strictly newest-to-oldest.
- **Date normalization:** an update with a full ISO timestamp (e.g. `"2026-08-07T00:00:00Z"`) is truncated to `"2026-08-07"` in the output.
- Assert `agentId`/`agentTitle` pass through unchanged so the page can link back to `/backlog/{agentId}`.

### Step 3: Build the `/changelog` page
**Files:** `app/changelog/page.tsx` (new)

- Server component (`async function` default export), no client state needed — same shape as `app/library/page.tsx` / `app/backlog/[agentId]/page.tsx`.
- Call `listChangelogEntries()` from `lib/changelog.ts`.
- Page chrome: `<main className="page-wrap page-wrap-wide">`, `page-title` = "Changelog", `page-subtitle` describing the combined feed.
- Feed list: reuse the existing "Updates" block styling from `app/backlog/[agentId]/page.tsx` (lines ~210-235) — `<ul className="mb-0 mt-3 list-none space-y-4 p-0">` with `<li className="border-t border-[var(--rule-soft)] pt-4 first:border-t-0 first:pt-0">` per entry, showing:
  - Meta line: `{entry.date} · <Link href={`/backlog/${entry.agentId}`}>{entry.agentTitle}</Link> · {entry.author}` styled `text-[13.5px] font-medium text-[var(--ink-faint)]`.
  - Note line styled `text-[15px] leading-6 text-[var(--ink-soft)]`.
  - Use a stable `key` combining `agentId`, `date`, and array index (dates/agents can repeat).
- Empty state: if `entries.length === 0`, render a "No updates yet" message (mirror the empty-state pattern in `app/library/page.tsx`'s "No matches yet" section, or the single-agent empty state in `app/backlog/[agentId]/page.tsx`).
- Design tokens only (`var(--ink)`, `var(--ink-soft)`, `var(--ink-faint)`, `var(--rule-soft)`, etc.) — no new colors/spacing values outside the existing CSS custom properties in `app/globals.css`.

### Step 4: Add the "Changelog" nav link
**Files:** `lib/garage-content.ts`

- Add `{ href: "/changelog", label: "Changelog" }` to the `"Explore"` group in `navGroups`, after the `"Backlog"` entry. `components/portal-nav.tsx` already derives its links from `navGroups` (`navGroups.flatMap(...)`), so no changes are needed there — the new link and active-state highlighting (via `pathname.startsWith(item.href)`) will work automatically.

### Step 5: Update architecture docs
**Files:** `docs/architecture.md`

- Add `/changelog` to the pages list in the architecture diagram (near `/backlog`, `/plan`) and mention `lib/changelog.ts` alongside the other `lib/` modules listed, so the doc keeps matching the shipped module layout (existing convention: this file enumerates every page + lib module).

---

## 🧪 Testing Strategy

- **Unit:** `tests/changelog.test.ts` as described in Step 2 — run via `npm run test` (Vitest).
- **Type/Lint:** `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` must pass — no `any`, follow existing type patterns (mirrors `AgentUpdate` typing conventions in `lib/backlog-meta.ts`).
- **Build:** `npm run build` must succeed with the new `/changelog` route statically/server-rendered like the other pages.
- **Manual:** Visit `/changelog` locally, confirm entries render newest-first, agent links navigate to `/backlog/{agentId}`, nav highlights "Changelog" when active, and the empty state renders correctly if the registry temporarily has zero updates (can spot-check by temporarily emptying an agent's `updates` array in a local manifest, without committing that change).

## ⚠️ Risks & Considerations

- **Schema currently requires `author`:** `parseUpdates` in `lib/agent-registry.ts` calls `requireString(entry, "author", file)`, which throws on manifests with a blank/missing author — so a real "unknown author" case can't occur via the registry today. The `buildChangelogFeed` fallback still needs to exist per the card's test requirement, but note in review that it's defensive/future-proofing rather than reachable through current YAML validation.
- **"All agents in the registry" scope:** shipped/library agents (`AgentLibraryEntry`) have no `updates[]` field at all today. This plan sources the feed from `backlogAgents` only, since that's the only place update history lives. If the intent was to eventually track updates on shipped agents too, that would need a separate follow-up to add `updates` to `AgentLibraryEntry`/`agent-library.ts` and the shipped-manifest validation branch in `lib/agent-registry.ts` — flagging this as an open question rather than in scope here.
- **Key uniqueness in the list:** with agents contributing multiple updates, `key` must combine agent id + date + index to stay stable and unique across re-renders.

actions.text:
📋 **Implementation Plan Ready**

I've created a detailed implementation plan with 6 steps covering:
- A new pure `listChangelogEntries()` data function (`lib/changelog.ts`) that flattens `updates[]` from every backlog agent into one newest-first feed, normalizing dates to `YYYY-MM-DD` and defaulting missing authors to "unknown"
- Unit tests for the required edge cases (no updates, same-date tiebreak by agent name, missing author)
- A new `/changelog` page reusing the existing Updates-list styling/tokens from `app/backlog/[agentId]/page.tsx`
- A nav link added via `lib/garage-content.ts` (no changes needed in `portal-nav.tsx` itself), plus an architecture doc update

One scope note flagged in the card: only backlog manifests (`scoped`/`claimed`/`in_build`) carry `updates[]` today — shipped/library agents have no update history in the schema — so the feed sources from `backlogAgents`. Review the updated description and move to TODO when ready to implement!

📋 **Stories Created**

I've broken down this feature's implementation plan into the following ordered, INVEST-sized user stories:

1. [As a visitor, I want a combined changelog data feed so that agent update history can be surfaced consistently](https://trello.com/c/7uABPulZ) — `lib/changelog.ts` + `tests/changelog.test.ts` (foundational, no UI)
2. [As a visitor, I want a /changelog page so that I can browse all agent updates in one place](https://trello.com/c/fbD6GceS) — new `app/changelog/page.tsx`, reusing the backlog detail page's Updates styling
3. [As a visitor, I want the Changelog linked in nav and docs so that I can discover it](https://trello.com/c/bzDu2nSL) — nav link in `lib/garage-content.ts` + `docs/architecture.md` update

**Recommended order:** #1 → #2 → #3 (each is independently shippable/green, but #2 needs #1's data function to exist, and #3 needs #2's page to exist before linking to it).

Each card has an "✅ Acceptance Criteria" checklist, and #2/#3 have a "🔗 Dependencies" checklist pointing back to their prerequisite stories.

Ready for review! 🚀
